current.text: He is the clear starting center for Atlanta. No established backup threatens his job.
Atlanta's center depth is thin: Veesaar is out for the season and Gueye is injured.
Atlanta is very cautious with his minutes.
Quin Snyder wants him spaced away from the rim when he plays with Daniels and Johnson.
Lloyd does not expect his FG% or his block rate to recover under Snyder. Another expert also doubts a FG% bounce back because Trae Young is still gone.
Experts call him fair value around picks 50 to 60s, mostly as a positional pick at center. Round 3 or 4 is too high, and nine-cat rankings make him look better than he is in category leagues.
Atlanta plays 4, 4 and 3 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21. The team has 14 back-to-backs and resting players is not a concern.

durable.text: He is a stretch center who makes threes on real volume. He also handles the ball better than most centers and has good hands and feel.
Playing on the perimeter gives him more threes and assists but fewer finishes at the rim and fewer offensive rebounds.
On defense he trades blocks for steals. He defends on the perimeter and cuts down on fouls.
Expect the same profile going forward, maybe with a few more blocks.
For a center, his threes and steals stand out. He has no weak category.
He is not a huge rebounder but is a usable second center. His broad line suits category leagues more than points leagues.

note: He is a clear starting center who helps in every build, with threes and steals that are rare for a center. Yahoo values him at 22 USD, but the average costs are 7.8 USD on Yahoo and 5.2 USD on ESPN, and our league paid 6 USD last season. Experts say nine-cat rankings (Yahoo 49, ESPN 44) overrate him, so pay close to the average cost, not the Yahoo value. Early in the season, check whether his FG% stays near 48% and his blocks near 1.1, and watch how Atlanta handles his minutes.
